one_liner: Eternal runs India's biggest apps for getting food, groceries, and other everyday stuff delivered fast, plus the B2B supply chain that feeds restaurants.

segments.name: Quick Commerce (Blinkit)
segments.description: 10-20 minute delivery of groceries, daily essentials, electronics and more from a growing network of dark stores; now the fastest-growing and largest revenue driver.

segments.name: India Food Ordering and Delivery (Zomato app)
segments.description: Marketplace connecting restaurants, delivery partners, and diners for food ordering and delivery; the original and most mature business, now roughly breakeven.

segments.name: Hyperpure Supplies (B2B)
segments.description: Supplies fruits, vegetables, meat, dairy, packaging and other ingredients to restaurant partners, plus 4PL warehousing; low-margin, volume-driven business.

segments.name: Going Out (District)
segments.description: Dining-out discovery, movie and event ticketing, and live events under the District app; smallest segment, still scaling.

unit_drivers.name: Gross Order Value (GOV) across food delivery and quick commerce
unit_drivers.note: Total value of orders placed; revenue is a take-rate cut of this. Company discloses GOV in investor presentations but not restated to a single confident FY2026 figure here.

unit_drivers.name: Number of active dark stores (Blinkit)
unit_drivers.note: Store count has been expanding aggressively (reported quarterly); drives both revenue growth and near-term margin drag from new-store losses.

unit_drivers.name: Average order value (AOV)
unit_drivers.note: Key lever for unit economics in both food delivery and quick commerce; company does not consistently disclose a single blended figure.

unit_drivers.name: Take rate / commission
unit_drivers.note: Effective monetization rate on food delivery and Blinkit orders; implied by revenue/GOV, varies by segment and is not separately confirmed here.

unit_drivers.name: Orders per day
unit_drivers.note: Volume driver disclosed periodically by management; not pinned down with confidence for FY2026.

addressable_market: India's online food delivery and quick commerce markets combined are estimated in the tens of billions of dollars (food delivery GOV roughly $8-10bn, quick commerce GOV growing even faster and potentially larger over time), within a broader ~$900bn+ Indian retail and foodservice opportunity that is still mostly offline.
competitive_position: Eternal (via Zomato) and Swiggy are the clear duopoly in Indian food delivery, each with roughly similar GOV share; in quick commerce, Blinkit competes intensely with Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, and newer entrants like Amazon/Flipkart-backed players in a land-grab phase. Moat comes from delivery-fleet density, dark-store network effects, and brand trust, but competitive intensity keeps margins thin and capex/opex high.
key_risks: Quick commerce (Blinkit) profitability depends on dark-store maturity and discipline on new-store losses; a prolonged price war with Swiggy Instamart/Zepto could keep margins negative longer than expected.
Regulatory risk around gig-worker classification, delivery partner wages, and potential restrictions on deep discounting or dark-store zoning could raise costs or cap growth.

Heavy reliance on continued hypergrowth (revenue roughly 2.7x in FY2026) to reach scale economics; any slowdown in order growth without margin improvement would pressure the current near-breakeven narrative.
industry_reason: The largest and fastest-growing piece of Eternal's revenue and operating losses now comes from Blinkit, an inventory-and-logistics-heavy quick commerce grocery/essentials retailer, not a pure asset-light software marketplace; its economics (warehousing, delivery fleet, thin take-rate margins) map most closely to the Retail (Grocery and Food) peer group rather than Software (Internet) or Restaurant/Dining.
